data.title: Selenium sulfide shampoo (1–2.5%)
data.summary: X Hair & scalp agents · Inorganic sulfide; cytostatic and antifungal
data.body:
_Topicals · X Hair & scalp agents_

**Class:** Inorganic sulfide; cytostatic and antifungal

## Mechanism of action
- Cytostatic — reduces epidermal (keratinocyte) turnover, so less scale
- Antifungal against Malassezia (sporicidal)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Pityriasis versicolor (2.5% as a body lotion/shampoo)
- Seborrhoeic dermatitis and dandruff
- Tinea capitis (adjunct, 2.5% twice weekly — reduces spore shedding and transmission)

## Dose & formulations
- Pityriasis versicolor: apply 2.5% to affected skin for 10 min daily for 7 days (or overnight once weekly), then monthly for prevention
- Scalp: leave 2–3 min, rinse; twice weekly for 2 weeks, then weekly

## Adverse effects
- Irritation (avoid broken skin, genitals), unpleasant smell
- Oily scalp, hair discolouration (orange tinge on grey/dyed hair), hair loss (rare)
- Absorption from broken skin can be toxic

## Contraindications
- Broken or inflamed skin; genital area

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid large-area use in pregnancy.

## Viva points
- Cytostatic + antifungal
- Used in tinea capitis to reduce spore shedding (adjunct to oral therapy)

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.51; Khopkar ch.19 and ch.28. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
